jp: 弟[おとうと]は毎朝[まいあさ]起[お]こしてもらう{くせに|pt-kuseni}、「自分[じぶん]で起[お]きた」と言[い]う。
en: My brother gets woken up every morning, yet he claims he got up by himself.
why: くせに criticises a gap between what he is and what he claims, with a note of blame.

jp: 母[はは]の料理[りょうり]は簡単[かんたん]な{わりに|pt-kuseni}、とてもおいしい。
en: My mother's cooking is very tasty for how simple it is.
why: わりに links a quality to a surprising result against what you would expect from it.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は小学生[しょうがくせい]{にしては/のわりに|pt-kuseni}背[せ]が高[たか]い。
en: My younger sister is tall for an elementary school student.
why: にしては compares someone with the standard for their category: tall for a schoolchild.

jp: 父[ちち]は休[やす]みの日[ひ]に何[なに]も手伝[てつだ]わない{くせに|pt-kuseni}、母[はは]に文句[もんく]を言[い]う。
en: My father does not help at all on his days off, yet he complains to my mother.
why: くせに blames someone for doing X despite not doing the expected thing.

jp: この家[いえ]は駅[えき]から遠[とお]い{わりに|pt-kuseni}、家賃[やちん]が高[たか]い。
en: This house is far from the station, yet the rent is high.
why: わりに says the result does not match what the first fact would lead you to expect.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]は八十歳[はちじゅっさい]{にしては/のわりに|pt-kuseni}元気[げんき]で、毎朝[まいあさ]散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]く。
en: My grandmother is energetic for eighty and goes for a walk every morning.
why: にしては measures her energy against what is normal for an eighty-year-old.

jp: 洗[あら]い物[もの]は全然[ぜんぜん]しない{くせに|pt-kuseni}、夫[おっと]は私[わたし]の料理[りょうり]に文句[もんく]ばかり言[い]う。
en: My husband never does the dishes, yet all he does is complain about my cooking.
why: くせに expresses irritation at someone who does nothing yet criticises.

jp: 兄[あに]は朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]をたくさん食[た]べた{わりに|pt-kuseni}、昼[ひる]にはもうおなかがすいたそうだ。
en: My brother ate a lot of breakfast, yet he reportedly was already hungry at noon.
why: わりに marks the unexpected result: a big breakfast should not leave him hungry so soon.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]八時間[はちじかん]寝[ね]ている{わりに|pt-kuseni}、朝[あさ]はいつも眠[ねむ]い。
en: I sleep eight hours a night, yet I am always sleepy in the morning.
why: わりに contrasts the expected result of good sleep with the actual sleepiness.

jp: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしを始[はじ]めたばかり{にしては/のわりに|pt-kuseni}、兄[あに]の部屋[へや]はきれいだ。
en: My brother's room is clean for someone who has just started living alone.
why: にしては judges the room against what is typical for a person who just moved out.

jp: 母[はは]は私[わたし]に「早[はや]く寝[ね]なさい」と言[い]う{くせに|pt-kuseni}、自分[じぶん]は夜中[よなか]までテレビを見[み]ている。
en: My mother tells me to go to bed early, yet she herself watches TV until the middle of the night.
why: くせに criticises the mismatch between what she says and what she does herself.
